question: What do omakit inspect, verify and submit say about Theme Manager before and after every QML process site goes through the Run block, and does the ported plugin still do what it did?
method: Three documents on the default branch HEAD (7239ae8, the commit the marketplace validated) and three on the run-port branch, with the same omakit checkout and pin; inspect after 6fd7154, which stopped counting an expression at argv[0] as a tool resolved from PATH (both sides re-measured with it). Counts only: no site list, since the plugin is a named repository. The desktop harness ran the ported controllers and the picker's Run sites in a separate quickshell instance under systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=768M, every action that does not change the desktop once, against temporary paths where a write was involved; the plugin's own tests/lab/acceptance.sh ran in the plugin lab's stock 4.0.3 guest at commit d9f6093 for the flows that change a desktop.
notes: process-lifecycle 23 and unbounded-buffering 18 are gone: every one of the 24 QML sites carries a deadline through the block and no collector without a cap remains.

The two file writes that were bash -c strings (the selection and done files) are FileView writes from the process itself, not Run sites: the done mark must survive the picker's destruction, and Run ends its group on destruction. The 26 sites inspect counted (23 Process, 3 execDetached) plus one Util.execArgv it did not see became 24 Run sites and 2 in-process writes.

environment-trust rose by 8 shell lines: the five new helpers name mkdir, cmp, cp, chmod, stat, readlink, flock, tr and gsettings bare, under Run's closed environment (docs/BLOCKS_SPIKE.md, the prelude decision); its QML part went from 13 sites to 0.
network-egress rose by 2: the hostile-fetch test's local http://127.0.0.1 server, in tests/.
file-and-state-boundary is unchanged at 7; the three new helpers create their one directory with mode 0700.
verify and submit are unchanged: review-required on the installer capability, listed.

The marketplace blocker at cc6486a (partial-clone git cat-file -s before the size check, unbounded tree and pack fetch) was replaced on main at e306998 by a bounded archive download; the port adds tests/theme-install-hostile.py, real repositories served over a local socket: an oversized blob refused after the inventory pass with nothing extracted, an oversized pack refused before a byte of body with a declared length and at the cap plus one 64 KiB read without one, a trickle stopped by the deadline with under 64 bytes landed.

omakit: 6fd7154 inspect: an argv word that is an expression is not a tool resolved from PATH
plugin: 7ac5a0c Add omakit's Run block 0.1.0 under omakit/
f1f8511 Start every program through Run: 27 sites ported, seven shell strings gone
d9f6093 Prove the bounded fetch against hostile repositories over a real socket
28d8ce8 Helpers: create their one directory with mode 0700

limits: One plugin, the author's own; the reviewer has not seen the port.
inspect's shell counts include the plugin's tests/ and lab scripts, which ship in the tree.
Time to end per site was not measured here; the lab suite's figures for the block itself are in 2026-09-17-run-lab-*.json.

closedEnvironmentReading.rule: A helper is a file of the tree that a Run site's argv[0] resolves to through the text: a literal or + chain, Qt.resolvedUrl and Quickshell.env, an identifier through its nearest assignment before the site or its property binding, a parent file's binding on the component, a same-file function through its return expression with the arguments in place. An argv[0] the text does not show (an array from a JavaScript module, a ternary of arrays, a function returning the array) resolves to nothing and marks nothing; a path under $OMARCHY_PATH is not the tree's. When every QML process site of the tree is a Run site, the shell lines of the resolved helpers carry closedEnvironment: true and the environment-trust class counts their tool names apart, in words. A line starting with exec is a process site.

superseded.rule: by base name in any QML string literal (phase 4)
superseded.why: it matched the plugin's own copy of list.sh, which the QML starts from Omarchy's tree, and every helper whose name appeared anywhere, whether or not a Run site reached it

closedEnvironmentReading.note: After the port, 12 of 24 Run sites resolve to a file of the tree, 9 distinct helpers, 50 tool names counted apart; 12 sites do not: 7 name programs outside the tree (/usr/bin/gsettings, /usr/bin/magick, /usr/bin/xdg-open, Omarchy's commands under omarchyBin, Omarchy's list.sh under $OMARCHY_PATH) and 5 carry an argv the text does not show (the two icons-browse.sh sites and the two aether sites from JavaScript model functions, install-wallpaper.sh from a function returning the array, reset-icons.sh from a ternary of arrays), so icons-browse.sh, install-wallpaper.sh and reset-icons.sh stay ambient although Run starts them. The two exec lines (catalog.sh, probe-theme-lock.sh) are sites now, on both sides.

provenance.session: The plugin-lab harness of that day passed --sync-all and --dev-link, so the guest's session ran from the omarchy checkout at b5589faaf80c6f87c07d4560fca37c4a81722f28 (the v4.0.3 tag plus merge #11263; 352 files differ from the tag, 70 of them under bin/, shell/ and config/) linked over the installed package, and the record did not know it (docs/history/2026-09-18-lab-inventory.md, P8). The installed packages were the 4.0.3 ISO's (omarchy 4.0.3-1 in the base's pacman.log of 2026-09-10; python 3.14.7, quickshell 0.3.1 read by the suite), and no run read the package version. Annotated 2026-09-18.
provenance.whatItMeans: The 27 acceptance steps exercised the session's shell (plugin add, the shortcuts, the theme and wallpaper apply), so they ran against the shell of checkout b5589fa, not the shell of the installed 4.0.3-1 package. They are evidence for the port on that checkout's shell; the claim 'on the stock guest' is withdrawn. Not re-measured: omakit lab runs this repository's suites and does not run a plugin's own acceptance (docs/LAB.md, what the lab does not do).
